summary: Plausible and a different lever from every earlier router attempt: it overlaps the graph's memset node with the router kernel (earlier attempts tuned the kernel or replaced the memset with a ticket epilogue). Deleting the memset at m<=8 saved 0.40-0.54 us, and PDL paid between our own kernels in decode. The in-prepare interleaved read-flush gate gives master vs candidate on identical surroundings; no companion. Tighten two guards: the PTX check must count exactly one griddepcontrol.wait, and the race check needs a slow-primary stand-in.
justification: Router rows at m=16/32/128/256 (5.48/5.95/7.95/9.51 us vs floors 1.8-2.7 us) are a fill node (0.7-0.9 us) plus the Triton split-K kernel with atomics. The m<=8 memset deletion (~0.4-0.5 us) is the realistic ceiling; m=128/256 predictions are ~0.2 us optimistic; a realistic 5-6% still clears drift and the 1.03 gate. Headline ~+0.3%, unreadable: judge on the four router rows and the R-PDL gate lines, not profile top_kernels (PDL-inflated rows). Prior router-splitk-semaphore-no-memset serialized the reduce; this keeps the relaxed atomics and the memset. Weakest link: whether Triton 3.8's launch_pdl under graph capture produces a real programmatic edge, and whether Triton auto-inserts a griddepcontrol.wait at entry; either gives a misleading flat result. Assert exactly one griddepcontrol.wait per router kernel (after the last mma, before the red/atom) and exactly one launch_dependents in the zero kernel at entry.
confounders: bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32: sets the K-loop available to hide the fill; a precondition shared by both arms.
router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m: the split-K atomic + zeros design; a precondition.
restack-three-cell-wins (router_kernel<8,8>, no memset at m<=8): m<=8 rows stay flat.
Queued router-hilo-m128-m256-readflush-config-sweep: same rows; keep separate checks; whichever lands second re-gates.
interference: No companion. Add a third gate arm (Triton zero kernel + router PDL=False, no launch_pdl) and print its net us beside cand/master, to separate the fill change from PDL.
rules_flags: No rule problems: torch.empty + own zero kernel in kernel_fn as master's torch.zeros; branches on cfg/shape/flags; no host syncs; precision unchanged.

Compile-in-capture risk: PDL is a constexpr and launch_pdl a compile option; warm every m class the judge can hit (ROUTER_WARM_MS 1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 plus m=9 and m=64) with the exact kernel_fn kwargs.
Replace any bitwise 'second launch identical' check with the tolerance compare (relaxed atomic order is nondeterministic).
open_questions: Does Triton 3.8 insert griddepcontrol.wait at entry with launch_pdl=True? Count waits and check position.
Race check: add a stand-in primary that spins ~10 us before storing zeros; a debug variant without the wait must fail.
Does graph capture keep the programmatic edge on the judge (cu130)? Print the edge type if cheap.
At m=256: 16 zero CTAs + 128 router CTAs at ~144 KB smem; confirm no placement delay.
Check both rounds' IQRs before trusting a marginal 1.03 pass.
